Bechina-equivalent language (identity declarations using 'אֵלּוּ', 'הֵם', Onkelos translations, and mirrored opposites) yields two thematic clusters: (1) the righteous teacher and Torah-as-inheritance [good], (2) the corrupt teacher and his disciples [evil]. packages.label: הֲלָכוֹת וְנַחֲלַת אָבוֹת
packages.reason: The central domain of Torah #103's positive teaching is the equation: הֲלָכוֹת (halakhot) ARE נַחֲלַת אָבוֹת (ancestral inheritance). The Gemara (Sanhedrin 91b) establishes this as an explicit identity — Torah/halakhot are not merely commanded but are the inheritance of Israel, received through the lineage of ancestors. The righteous teacher (מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים) who transmits halakhot to his students is identified in Bava Batra 8b as מְלַמְּדֵי תִּינוֹקוֹת (children's teachers), and they are compared to the stars (כַּכּוֹכָבִים) — an explicit bechina-equivalence using 'אֵלּוּ' (these are...). Stars are the bechina of the teachers who make many righteous, because they illuminate the night and give light to many. The dominant node is הֲלָכוֹת (the teaching content = the inheritance) because the entire teaching pivots on whether halachic content is transmitted or withheld. Good/evil mirror: the good teacher who gives halakhot (this package) is the mirror of the corrupt teacher who withholds/steals them (Package 2).

merge_notes.reason: These three form a tight bechina cluster: Bava Batra 8b declares 'מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים כַּכּוֹכָבִים — אֵלּוּ מְלַמְּדֵי תִּינוֹקוֹת'. The 'אֵלּוּ' is the classical bechina-declaration formula: these (stars) = these (teachers). All three — the act of making-many-righteous, the role of children's teacher, and the star-symbol — share the same essential nature: the teacher who freely transmits Torah/halakhot to many students and thereby righteous them. They belong in Package 1 because the defining shared nature is positive transmission of halakhot (= nachalat avot).

Sanhedrin 91b equates these directly: 'הֲלָכוֹת הֵם נַחֲלַת אָבוֹת'. This is not cause-and-effect; it is an identity statement. Halakhot ARE the inheritance — they are two names for the same reality: the Torah content that passes from generation to generation as a sacred patrimony. The shared nature is: Torah-knowledge-as-patrimony.

packages.label: תַּרְבּוּת אֲנָשִׁים חַטָּאִים
packages.label_en: Brood of Sinful Men — The Corrupt Teacher Cluster
packages.reason: The evil mirror of Package 1. Where Package 1 is the teacher who transmits Torah-as-inheritance, Package 2 is the teacher who withholds or steals it. The text explicitly names this cluster using Moses's condemnation: תַּרְבּוּת אֲנָשִׁים חַטָּאִים (Numbers 32:14), which Onkelos translates as תַּלְמִידֵי גֻּבְרַיָּא חַיָּבַיָּא (disciples of wicked men). These two phrases are explicit bechina-equivalences (the Hebrew verse and its Aramaic translation name the same essential reality). The evil teacher's actions are described through two more bechina-equivalent phrases: מְחַיְּבֵי הָרַבִּים (those who make many guilty — the exact evil mirror of מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים) and מְנִיאֵי לֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (those who dissuade the hearts of Israel from their inheritance). Both phrases name the same essential reality from different angles: the teacher who corrupts rather than rectifies his students. The Rebbe applies this to teachers who 'stole halakhot' from students — גּוֹזֵל נַחֲלַת אָבוֹת (robber of ancestral inheritance) is the identity assigned to such a teacher. Dominant node: מְחַיְּבֵי הָרַבִּים (most structurally connected, as it is the direct evil counterpart of מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים which is the dominant-adjacent node in Package 1).

merge_notes.reason: These are the same condemnation in two languages: the biblical Hebrew (Numbers 32:14) and Onkelos's Aramaic translation. Onkelos's translation is an explicit bechina-equivalence — the targum declares what the Hebrew 'IS' in meaning. Both name the same essential reality: the student-group shaped by a wicked teacher. Shared nature: the disciple-body that carries forward the corruption of its teacher, perpetuating the theft of Torah from Israel.

These are two descriptions of the same action of the evil teacher: 'making many guilty' and 'dissuading the hearts of Israel from their ancestral inheritance'. They are not cause-and-effect (one does not produce the other); they are two faces of the same reality. The teacher who dissuades Israel IS the one who makes them guilty. Shared nature: the destructive-teacher action that corrupts the many.

The Gemara states the teacher who withholds halakha IS as if he robbed the student of the ancestral inheritance ('כְּאִלּוּ גּוֹזְלוֹ מִנַּחֲלַת אָבוֹת'). The Rebbe drops the 'כְּאִלּוּ' (as if) and treats this as a real identity — the withholding-teacher IS a robber of inheritance. This node belongs in the evil package because it names the essential nature of the corrupt teacher from the perspective of the damage done: he is, at his core, a thief of Torah-patrimony.
